title: 7-day KPI habit sprint — weekly scratchpad
content:
Goal: run a focused 7-day habit sprint to lock in small changes that move one personal KPI: weekly deep-work hours (target = +3 hours/week -> from 7 to 10).

Context / why now:
- Q1 context: busy with oncall rotation + shipping the batching patch, energy and focus slipped. Want a small low-friction experiment to regain rhythm.
- Downstream wins: more uninterrupted time -> faster PR reviews, clearer design writeups, fewer context switches for the serving-runtime kernel selection work.

This doc = daily scratchpad + quick metrics snapshot + micro-retrospective at end of week. Informal notes to self.

Day 0 (prep) — Mon 2026-03-09
- Baseline: last 7 days deep-work = ~7 hours (calendar blocks tagged 'deep' + manual tally).
- Commitment: 3x 90-minute morning blocks + 1x 60-minute evening block across the next 7 days.
- Tools: Pomodoro timer, calendar blocks named "Deep — Noelle", block notifications set to silent.
- Quick TODOs:
  * Add calendar event template (done)
  * Create short Slack away message (draft below)
  * Pin tickets to focus board: GH PR #742, JIRA-OPS-1983, CONFLUENCE: ENG-OKR-2026

Day 1 — Tue 2026-03-10
- Result: two 90-min morning blocks completed (3.0h), evening block skipped (0h).
- Observations: best focus window is 9:00–11:00, after coffee. Afternoon still noisy (standups & syncs).
- What went well: little email/Slack interruptions in morning.
- Friction: late meeting (1pm) pushed afternoon energy down.
- Quick note: when in deep block, set Slack to DND for entire block (not just 30 min).

Day 2 — Wed 2026-03-11
- Result: one 90-min morning block + one 60-min evening block = 2.5h. Cumulative = 5.5h.
- Wins: finished draft of design doc for lightweight KV cache invalidation in private deployments. Linked to GH PR #742 for context.
- Hypothesis: evening blocks are less reliable due to personal context; move one morning block earlier to 8am?

Day 3 — Thu 2026-03-12
- Result: two morning blocks done + scheduled 60-min block (done) = 4.5h that day (cumulative 10h). Hit target earlier than expected.
- Metric note: felt higher quality output during uninterrupted 90-min kernel profiling session.
- Quick metrics to track from work context (personal but tied to product):
  * Prefix cache hit rate experiment: target > 45% on sample traffic for this prototype. Current baseline = 31%.
  * Median P99 latency for local bench (gpt-medium variant): baseline 98ms, aim to shave 5–10ms by micro-optimizations.
  * Token cost per 1k on dev traffic: baseline $0.92, target <$0.80 if caching helps.

Day 4 — Fri 2026-03-13
- Result: lighter day, 1.5h only. Cumulative 11.5h.
- Reflection: momentum matters more than perfect adherence.
- Action: plan a quick "focus hygiene" checklist to reuse next sprint.

Micro-retro (end of 7-day sprint) — Sat 2026-03-14
- Final tally: deep-work = 12.0 hours (goal hit: +5 hours vs baseline).
- What changed: earlier calendar blocks + strict DND = biggest lever.
- What to keep (habits to persist):
  * 2x guaranteed 90-min morning blocks on Mon/Wed/Thu (calendar-only blocks).
  * Slack DND for full block + short away message with clear fallback.
  * Move non-urgent meetings to afternoons or Fridays where possible.
- What to drop: evening blocks — low yield, inconsistent.

Concrete follow-ups (personal + product-oriented):
- Personal: set recurring template for morning deep blocks (calendar) and a short SOP for family coordination re: evening availability. (ETA: 2026-03-21)
- Product: pair with Mikael to A/B backend caching knob: 2 configs (prefetch vs strict eviction) and measure prefix cache hit rate on the canary workload. Track in CONFLUENCE page ENG-OKR-2026. (Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/742)
- Ops: add a small perf benchmark job to CI to measure median P99 on the gpt-medium variant nightly. File JIRA ticket: JIRA-OPS-1983.

Open questions / scribbles:
- Can we get a cheap metric for user-visible quality change due to caching? (e.g., regeneration rate, hallucination signals)
- If evening blocks fail, would micro-blocks (25-min Pomodoro x3) preserve momentum without family friction?
- How to align focus blocks with oncall calendar: maybe tag oncall as 'critical' only for urgent pages, otherwise DND.

Quick templates / snippets (for reuse)
- Slack away message: "In a focused block until {end_time}. If urgent, DM 'urgent-{team}' or call. I will respond after {end_time}."
- Calendar description template:
  "Deep — Noelle (do not schedule): goal = uninterrupted focus on servicing runtime profiling or design. Set Slack DND. Primary outputs: PR drafts, perf dashboard updates, confluence notes."

Experiment notes (brief)
- Cache-prefetch experiment (local): run 10k synthetic requests with sequence length distribution sampled from production sample v2. Measure prefix cache hit rate, end-to-end median latency.
- Quick result (local run): prefix hit 34% -> shaving 7ms median latency. Need canary on dedicated to confirm.

Logistics / tiny wins to follow up next week:
- Add focus tags to calendar events for automatic tallying.
- Share micro-retro with Ravi + Mikael for alignment; ask for pairing slot next week (30–60m).
- If consistent, tag habit as recurring in personal tracker and review monthly.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally messy. The point is low-friction capture and rapid iteration. If a habit survives two 7-day sprints, consider promoting to calendar default.

End.
